items.title: Section: The Tenth and Final Ground Opens — Ready to Become Dharma-King, Recalling the Ninth Ground's Ten Dhāraṇīs of a Great Teacher (continued)

items.zh: 於一切住菩薩行中，當知菩薩略有六種。於諸有情無倒攝受。何等為六？一者、頓普攝受，二者、增上攝受，三者、攝取攝受，四者、長時攝受，五者、短時攝受，六者、最後攝受。云何菩薩於諸有情頓普攝受？謂諸菩薩初發心時，攝受一切諸有情界皆為眷屬。作是思惟：我當於彼隨能隨力，作一切種利益安樂饒益之事。隨所思惟，皆如是作。是名菩薩於諸有情頓普攝受。云何菩薩於諸有情增上攝受？謂諸菩薩或為家主，攝受父母、妻子、奴婢、僮僕、作使；或為國王，攝受一切所統僚庶。菩薩如是發起增上攝受想已，於所攝受，隨攝受儀、隨菩薩儀業用而轉。若為家主，於其父母，種種方便勸修諸善；隨時供養，曾無懈廢；善識其恩，善知酬報；於父母心善能隨順；於法於義隨自在轉。於其妻子、奴婢等類，隨時恣與如法衣食；於諸事業終不逼切；雖有違犯，而能堪忍；彼若疾病，正能瞻療；於諸善事勸令修習；隨時賜與殊勝財物，愛語慰喻；不生奴婢、作使等想，瞻敬養育其若自身。若為國王，不行黜罰，不用刀杖，而能正化；以法以財用作饒益；依本土田而自食用，不以凶力侵掠他境；隨能隨力於諸有情勸止諸惡，教修諸善；視諸眾生，如父於子；於他有情尚好等施，況自親屬而不均濟；不行欺誑，所言誠諦；遠離一切殺縛、捶打、治罰、逼迫、斷截等事。是名菩薩於諸有情增上攝受。云何菩薩於諸有情攝取攝受？謂諸菩薩正御徒眾，當知是名略說菩薩於諸有情攝取攝受。若廣說者，由二因緣正攝徒眾，說名菩薩於諸有情攝取攝受。何等為二？一者、以無染心正攝徒眾；二者、於自義利正教修習，非邪加行而陷逗之。又於一切應攝受中，其心平等，不墮偏黨；亦不於彼慳悋正法，不作師捲；不於彼所悕求承事恭敬供養；彼樂善故，自求作者，亦不遮止。為欲令其福德資糧得增長故；或遇餘時，亦於彼所承事供養。若於其義未解了者，開悟令解；已解了者，轉令明淨。生起疑惑，隨為除斷。若生惡作，善為開解。甚深義句，以慧通達，於時時間正為開顯。於苦於樂與彼共同。於他所為財利因緣，成就上品經營遽務，過於自事。於他毀犯，隨時正舉令其覺悟，應時如理訶責、擯罰。彼有疹疾，或有愁憂，終不棄捨，善權方便救療疹疾、開解愁憂。於諸下劣形色、憶念、精進、智等，終不輕陵。於時時間，隨入勞倦，如其所宜為說正法。於時時間，為令繫念於所緣境，與正教授。堪忍問難，不生憤發。於彼戒行或等或增，終無減劣；亦不悕求利養恭敬；具足悲愍；無掉無動；戒、見、軌則、正命圓滿；舒顏平視，遠離顰蹙，柔和美語，先言問訊，含笑為先；於諸善品恒常修習，不行放逸，離諸懈怠。即以是事教習徒眾，亦令自行轉更勝進。菩薩不應於一切時攝取徒眾，亦非不攝，亦非變異。是名菩薩於諸有情攝取攝受。云何菩薩於諸有情長時攝受？謂諸菩薩，於住下品成熟有情攝受饒益，當知說名長時攝受，以經久時方堪淨故。云何菩薩於諸有情短時攝受？謂諸菩薩，於住中品成熟有情攝受饒益，當知說名短時攝受，非經久時方堪淨故。云何菩薩於諸有情最後攝受？謂諸菩薩，於住上品成熟有情攝受饒益，當知說名最後攝受，即於此生堪任淨故。是名菩薩於諸有情略有六種無倒攝受。由此攝受，過去、未來、現在菩薩，於諸有情曾正攝受、當正攝受、現正攝受。除此無有若過若增。

blocks.text: The chapter on "gathering in" (攝受) is one of the most practical passages in the whole treatise: how a bodhisattva should treat family, employees, subjects, and students. **All of today's Chinese is untranslated.**

items: **Six ways.** All at once and universal; by authority; taking in followers; long-term; short-term; and final.
**All at once.** At the first arousal of bodhicitta, the bodhisattva takes the whole realm of beings as family, and resolves to benefit them as far as their ability allows.

**By authority: as head of a household.** Towards parents: encourage them in good ways, support them without lapse, know and repay their kindness, accord with their wishes. Towards spouse, children, and servants: provide food and clothing in season; never drive them hard; bear with their faults; nurse them when ill; encourage good; give gifts and kind words; "not thinking of them as servants, but caring for them as for oneself".

**By authority: as a king.** No harsh dismissals or punishments, no weapons; govern by Dharma and by wealth; live from one's own lands and never invade others; regard beings "as a father regards his children"; be honest; avoid killing, imprisoning, beating, and mutilation.

**Taking in followers** (leading students). With an untainted mind, and teaching them for their own good, never by wrong methods. Be impartial; never hoard the Dharma or keep a "teacher's closed fist"; do not seek their service, though if they wish to serve for their own merit, do not forbid it. Explain what they do not understand and clarify what they half understand; remove doubts and remorse; share their joys and sorrows; work for their material needs more than for one's own; correct their faults at the right time; never abandon them in sickness or sorrow; never look down on those weaker in looks, memory, diligence, or intelligence; teach when they are tired; give meditation instruction; bear their questions without irritation. Be equal or better in conduct; seek no gain; "relaxed face, level gaze, no frowning, gentle words, greeting first, a smile before speaking". Train the students by one's own example. A bodhisattva should not always take students, nor never, nor be changeable.
**Long-term, short-term, final.** Caring for beings of low maturity takes a long time; for middling maturity, less; for high maturity, they are purified in this very life.

blocks.text: Anyone who teaches will recognise much here; so will anyone who has had a good teacher. "Greeting first, a smile before speaking" sounds simple. The treatise counts it as part of the bodhisattva path.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how should a bodhisattva who is head of a household regard servants and workers?
options: Not as servants, but caring for them as for oneself
With strict discipline at all times
quiz.why: "Not thinking of them as servants, caring for and supporting them as for oneself."

quiz.q: What does "the teacher's closed fist" (師捲) refer to?
options: Holding back part of the teaching from students
quiz.why: The bodhisattva teacher is "not stingy with the true Dharma" and keeps nothing back.

quiz.q: Which beings are cared for by "final" gathering in?
options: Those of high maturity, who can be purified in this very life
quiz.why: "Final" gathering in is for beings of the highest maturity.
